approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from the current session’s accepted molecules. It retains the highest-scoring breeders, samples parents by score quantile, and constructs fresh offspring using connected-fragment crossover and ordinary graph mutations. Stable canonical identities, duplicate checks and a source-relative sulfur rule determine admission to each full pool. A Gaussian process trained on the complete accepted archive uses integer Morgan environment counts to predict scores and correlated uncertainty; successive sampled function maxima choose the batch that receives real feedback.
approach.novelty: This control removes candidate-specific predictive location from successful pool allocation: every candidate receives the same archive-average location while keeping the exact original correlated residual draws. It isolates the contribution of learned relative location within the existing selector. Earlier siblings removed the whole allocation rule, removed residual sampling, replaced count means with binary means, or supplied pretrained means; none measured this location-presence contrast with the original residual geometry still active. The expected result is an exposed change in selected molecules and a possible loss of productive progress, which would support retaining predictive location.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent n-1744a1494180 has complete actual summary.json/run.log pairs: mean 0.59645311428869, population SD 0.03397032998399878, seed macros 0.643098123844866/0.563172834083287/0.583088384937917. Its accepted-score search delivers 648 strict best-parent wins, positive gain sum 17.251535 and sequential incumbent gain sum 5.819415, but successful replacement of its local predictive guidance remains unachieved. The specific research obstacle is that current evidence cannot separate learned candidate-location influence from its retained correlated residual allocation. Full-selector prefix control n-605c7a785b51 loses 0.12818290031998167, with seed deltas -0.206021671201779/-0.07253471860356697/-0.10599231115459906 and fourteen losing cells plus positive zaleplon seed 1. Mean-only n-f04cec6ab705 loses 0.1163168819901173, with seed deltas -0.226801804126509/-0.039889707510842/-0.082259134333001 and twelve losing cells plus gains on median_2 seeds 0/2 and sitagliptin seed 1. Neither answers location presence conditional on residuals. Binary-location n-161b32768a03 loses 0.08822718632415433, seed deltas -0.07425859425061199/-0.14939161486950597/-0.04103134985234502, twelve losing cells and gains on docking seed 0, sitagliptin seed 1 and zaleplon seed 2. Binary-residual n-b77e5493be1e loses 0.03715967951388403 with seed signs loss/gain/loss (-0.07507082794692899/+0.0026208679018949743/-0.039029078496618075), nine losing and six gaining endpoints. These support count information under their distinct literal consumers without identifying the present contrast. Exact-lock restored-GP control n-fe734eb5c1df gains 0.051679 over its external-mean Parent, with three positive seed macros and fourteen gains but negative median_2 seed 1; its trajectories reproduce the Anchor and supply no independent replication. MoLFormer n-61c472c961cc changes 2368/4350 choices but loses 0.06811086167142866, all seed macros (-0.094788450845693/-0.027975019848437/-0.081569114320156), ten losing and five gaining endpoints, despite 700 local wins versus 648. The bounded ablation asks whether candidate-specific location itself supplies useful adaptive direction; none of these recipe differences proves over-exploitation or authorizes a model/scale rescue.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse r33-persistent-niche-breeding-and-location-review under the unchanged Parent, current panel and exact inherited environment. Its observed bottleneck and deferral of unsupported encoder/kernel upgrades still fit. Direct full-selector, residual-only, binary-consumer and fixed external-location results leave this narrow presence contrast unanswered. Continue the existing selector contribution approach for one fixed constant-location control, then end after a complete naturally exposed answer; preserve unresolved contribution after incomplete/unexposed execution and do not start a blend, residual-scale or model sweep.
literature_review.internal_evidence_reason: The frozen bottleneck review’s primary-source search is reused, with its actual recorded query log. This removal is derived from direct current-Parent component/recipe evidence and does not adopt a new literature algorithm. Persistent MAP-Elites is assigned to the separate breeder position; exact kernel swaps, random features and newer TabPFN assets are deferred. No paper supplies evidence that constant location will improve endpoints.

hypothesis: Remove candidate-dependent original count-GP predictive location only at successful fresh-pool allocation by setting every active sample row to original_archive_score_mean + original_score_scale*(original_normals @ original_count_pool_factor.T), while retaining the exact original correlated residuals, complete passive count-GP computations and all generation, admission, breeding and accepted-feedback rules.

finding_summary.headline: Removing learned GP location changed search and lowered all 15 endpoints
finding_summary.insights: Candidate-dependent GP location has positive conditional value when the original correlated residuals, count representation, sulfur gate and breeder policy are retained. This is a complete answer to the registered location-presence contrast, not proof of total selector value or of how location and residuals mediate the effect. The original passive GP still ordered the same selected labels substantially better than the active constants: pair accuracy was 0.799 versus 0.500, while constant within-batch Spearman was undefined. That rules out missing or constant original predictions as an explanation for the loss. Broader structural output did not translate into productive exploration: first-arriving typed cores increased from 1,820 to 2,537 across sessions, yet parent-beating gain and incumbent progress fell. Chemistry helps describe the change in output: molecules with at most five heavy atoms increased from 105 to 612, aromatic-containing observations decreased, and oversized recombinations and reactive groups remained. These associations do not establish a chemical mediator or justify a universal fragment or functional-group ban. The retained GP location appears to supply useful adaptive direction beyond correlated residual exploration under this fixed panel. The pathway test should end with this answer; its registration supports no blend, scale or model rescue. Broader mechanism contribution, transfer to other conditions, physical feasibility and independent replication remain open.
finding_summary.results: The removal operated in every session: all 435 pools retained nonconstant original GP predictions but used one constant active location, with the original correlated residuals preserved. It changed 3,733 of 4,350 strict masked choices and placed 3,631 accepted molecules outside the passive original selected sets. Changed choices entered later fits and produced actual accepted descendants in all 15 sessions. Mean endpoint score fell from 0.596453 to 0.413485, a paired loss of 0.182968; every task–seed endpoint and all three seed averages declined. Seed-average population spread increased from 0.033970 to 0.072847. Useful progress weakened: strict parent-beating offspring fell from 648 to 414, their positive gain total from 17.251535 to 11.477453, and sequential incumbent gain from 5.819415 to 3.074901. Local gain totals nevertheless rose in all three zaleplon sessions, deco_hop seed 1 and docking seed 2; those exceptions did not produce an endpoint gain.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich output spans tiny fragments and elaborate polycycles; high scores still coexist with reactive groups and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: This assessment concerns n-04741f9b1832 versus published Parent n-1744a1494180 on the supplied frozen Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, with 300 observations per task and seed, including the ten initial observations. All 15 Child and 15 Parent indexed trajectory files were read: 4500 observations per side, including 4350 optimizer observations. No trajectory path is missing and no task comparison is absent. The brief explicitly reports both child_complete=true and paired_complete=true. The registered Child condition is constant-location allocation with the original correlated residuals and sulfur-gated graph generator retained; that condition identifies this evidence and is not an activation finding. Per-task seed comparisons below are descriptive molecular associations; no component, activation, mediation or selection conclusion is drawn. The digest pools seeds and its final excerpt contains only seed 2; the complete trajectories supply the other seed leaders and terminal observations. Across optimizer output, RDKit 2023.09.6 parses all 4350 Child structures and all 4350 Parent structures. Child has rings in 3506 and aromatic atoms in 2869 observations, versus 4239 and 4213 in Parent. Child contains 612 observations with at most five heavy atoms and 99 with at least 50, versus 105 and 48 in Parent. Thus ring-rich here describes substantial fused, bridged and heterocyclic chemistry within a heterogeneous set, not universal ring content. The five Child tasks have 522, 492, 416, 590 and 435 distinct nonempty typed Bemis-Murcko cores in the brief task order; these graph counts indicate broad structural variation, not useful exploration or synthesizability. The digest rates cited below are SMILES-text incidence counters; they are not fractions of atoms or RDKit aromatic-ring counts. All digest charge and tetrahedral-stereocentre token rates are zero. Independently, no Child optimizer graph carries a formal charge or tetrahedral chiral tag, while RDKit flags at least one unassigned potential tetrahedral centre in 2316 observations. Neutral notation does not establish protonation at any pH, and the graph flag does not establish an isolable stereoisomer. Graph SMARTS find O-O bonds in 224 Child versus 127 Parent observations, N-halogen bonds in 253 versus 786, O-halogen bonds in 207 versus 217, and carbon-centred cumulated double bonds in 32 versus 12. These overlapping structural alerts are not measured instability or toxicity; the Parent is not a chemical-safety reference. No synthetic route, conformer strain, pKa, logP, exposure, pharmacology or experimental feasibility was evaluated. The quality labels are cautious structural readings. All numerical descriptors are recomputed from the indexed SMILES, with exact patterns, row-level results, and source hashes retained in .slots/L01-resume-20261004/r33-slot1-molecular/measurements.json and the accompanying measured trajectory files. Only Child SMILES from the trusted request are quoted in cited_smiles; Parent structures are described from the published trajectories.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 optimizer observations range from 1 to 50 heavy atoms (median 22), with median three RDKit rings and one aromatic ring. Digest ring-closure and aromatic-token incidence are 0.8506 and 0.7034. The seed-0 leader is a 24-heavy-atom pyrazoline-like N-N ring bearing an N-hydroxy thiocarbonyl substituent, a phenyl group and a bridged unsaturated hydroxy carbocycle. Seed 1 leads with a 25-heavy-atom thioacetylated N-N heterocycle, fluorophenyl ketone and a seven-membered unsaturated N/OH-containing ring. Seed 2 leads with a 26-heavy-atom thioacetylated partially unsaturated N ring, fluorophenyl amide and hydroxypyridyl substituent. These are distinct chemical branches, not one shared aromatic scaffold. The common initial best is a trimethoxy indole carboxanilide at 0.305104808. Parent leaders instead retain fused aromatic N heterocycles with amide/hydroxamate-like or carbonyl-thione substitution and three perceived aromatic rings. In seed order 0/1/2, best observed Child scores are 0.423482167, 0.410039276, 0.391736055; published Parent best scores are 0.459357349, 0.474117018, 0.436954227. The last evaluated molecules score 0.204517869, 0.245629079, 7.84427568e-18 in that seed order; these are final observations, not final Top-1 values.
liabilities: N-hydroxy thiocarbonyl, adjacent N-N, enolic and bridged unsaturated environments warrant chemical review; their presence is not proof of instability or impossibility.
37 observations contain O-O and 77 O-halogen bonds, and 105 are at most five heavy atoms. Valence-valid graph admission includes chemistry far outside the compact leaders.
missing_features: Consistent preservation of compact, conjugated heteroaromatic/carbonyl arrangements is underrepresented relative to Parent: Child has aromatic atoms in 612/870 observations versus 843/870, and median one versus three aromatic rings. The Child can produce aromatic chemistry, so this is a distributional shortfall, not inability.
The leaders leave potential tetrahedral geometry unspecified. No trajectory evidence identifies a particular stereoisomer or additional functional group that would close the score gap.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Medium-sized, heteroatom-substituted ring assemblies outperform collapsed fragments: OBr at seed 0 evaluation 274 scores 0, and terminal CNO at seed 2 scores 7.844275678569281e-18. Excessive elaboration also fails: the seed-2 evaluation-298 polycycle scores 2.515691941645922e-17. Within seed 0, the unbridged phenolic N-hydroxy thiocarbonyl analogue at evaluation 89 scores 0.364931948, while the bridged leader scores 0.423482167; its additional fluorinated analogue at evaluation 223 scores 0.399247928. These individual comparisons do not show a monotone benefit from bridge formation or fluorination. Parent aromatic leaders have higher observed scores, but the trajectory does not isolate aromaticity, sulfur or any single functional group as the reason.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 optimizer observations span 1-99 heavy atoms (median 25), median three rings and two aromatic rings; digest ring-closure/aromatic-token incidence is 0.8069/0.7782. Seed 0 reaches a compact 19-heavy-atom fluorinated amino-acetal-like heterocycle linked to a fused N-containing ring system, including a four-membered perceived ring. Seed 1 leads with a 29-heavy-atom fused O/N carbonyl heteroaromatic scaffold and a conjugated amino-dinitrile connection to fluoropyridyl chemistry. Seed 2 leads with a much larger 44-heavy-atom assembly containing several fused amino heterocycles, an O-O-containing linker, O-Cl and N-Br attachments. The shared initial best scores 0.548381483. The Parent seed-0 leader at evaluation 297 is a compact fused N-rich carbonyl-thione heterocycle with additional O-F/chlorinated substituents; Parent seed 1 has an aromatic carbonyl/nitrile series and seed 2 an N-rich fused aromatic/nitroso-containing series. These higher Parent scores are not evidence of cleaner chemistry. In seed order 0/1/2, best observed Child scores are 0.588271031, 0.599987694, 0.583318157; published Parent best scores are 0.856147722, 0.620437688, 0.644233965. The last evaluated molecules score 0.524738868, 0.533785184, 0.525001405 in that seed order; these are final observations, not final Top-1 values.
liabilities: 102 observations contain O-O bonds, 130 N-halogen and 79 O-halogen bonds. The seed-2 leader combines these environments, and the seed-1 near-leader contains a hydroperoxy group.
135 observations have at most five heavy atoms; 37 have at least 50. Broad size and ring variation, including tightly connected small rings, does not demonstrate synthetic plausibility.
missing_features: The Child lacks a sampled high-score compact carbonyl-thione/fused-N arrangement matching the Parent seed-0 branch; carbonyl-bearing observations number 424/870 versus 832/870 in Parent. This is an observed population difference, not a prescription to reproduce the Parent structure.

Regular, chemically interpretable linkers and sustained intact ring substitution are inconsistent: seed 2 elaborates O-O/O-halogen/N-halogen connections while many observations lose the ring framework entirely. No specific absent pharmacophore is established.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The observed floor of 0.5 includes tiny fragments such as C#CC at seed 1 evaluation 296. Connected heteroaromatic and substituted fused-ring structures rise above that floor, but the best Child scores remain clustered around 0.58-0.60 despite very different molecular sizes and functional groups. In seed 1 the hydroperoxy analogue at evaluation 232 scores 0.595065514, close to the 0.599987694 leader; the score does not strongly penalize that O-O attachment in this comparison. The late Parent seed-0 0.856147722 molecule remains part of the full comparison. Nothing in the Child structures alone identifies the missing chemical change responsible for that larger Parent value.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 optimizer observations span 1-95 heavy atoms (median 17.5), with median two rings and one aromatic ring. Digest ring-closure/aromatic-token incidence is 0.7195/0.5851. Seed 0 leads with a 25-heavy-atom methylamino/N-methylazetidine arrangement attached to a fluorinated methoxy arene and a bridged unsaturated carbocycle. Seed 2 leads with a 24-heavy-atom polyamine/fused-ring assembly attached to a dihydroxy thiophenol ring. Seed 1 remains chemically different: its 36-heavy-atom leader contains a densely fused sulfonamide/lactam/amine framework and chlorinated unsaturation. The initial best is only 0.019041151. Parent leaders on all seeds combine amine-bearing ring or linker systems with substituted aromatic rings; Parent seed 1 reaches a much simpler diazepane-like/aromatic arrangement than the Child seed-1 polycycle. In seed order 0/1/2, best observed Child scores are 0.876893211, 0.093527931, 0.818441990; published Parent best scores are 0.991253913, 0.999999453, 0.981797584. The last evaluated molecules score 0.577011972, 0.0334356555, 0.0107001688 in that seed order; these are final observations, not final Top-1 values.
liabilities: The seed-0 leader contains an azetidine and bridged unsaturation; the seed-1 leader is a dense multiring sulfonamide/lactam graph. Their conformational strain and synthetic access have not been measured.

A high seed-0 near-leader at evaluation 295 scores 0.823796237 despite an N-Cl substituent. The seed-2 leader contains a thiol and adjacent phenolic functionality. High objective values do not remove these chemical questions.
missing_features: Amine/aromatic arrangements associated with the stronger seeds are not consistently retained in seed 1. The Child emits 169 observations with at most five heavy atoms and has aromatic atoms in only 509/870, versus 18 tiny observations and 846/870 aromatic-containing observations in Parent.

Resolved stereochemistry and evidence about geometrically accessible amine/aryl placement are absent. The generator can make amine-containing rings; a blanket claim that basic centres are missing would be false.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The strong Child seeds favour aromatic groups linked to accessible amine-like nitrogen environments over the initial sulfonyl/acyl-rich branch. The comparatively open seed-2 polyamine/thiophenol molecule at evaluation 160 scores 0.705339113 before its more fused 0.818441990 leader. In contrast, the N-chloro sulfonamide/carboxamide at seed 2 evaluation 20 scores 0.00016650955053713697 and a chlorinated aromatic ester/acid at seed 1 evaluation 95 scores 0.0004884065818939657. Seed 1 shows that increasing ring count and retaining nitrogen are insufficient: its best score remains 0.093527931. This is a structure-score association within the trajectories, not evidence of receptor binding, a protonation state or a validated pose.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 optimizer observations span 1-65 heavy atoms (median 23), with median three rings and one aromatic ring; digest ring-closure/aromatic-token incidence is 0.8655/0.754. Seed 0 leads with a 31-heavy-atom quinoline-like arene connected through an S-O linkage to a lactam/spiro amine-containing framework. Seed 1 leads with a 22-heavy-atom ethoxy-substituted fused arene and a cyclic N-N/dicarbonyl unit carrying N-Cl. Seed 2 leads with a 27-heavy-atom fused dicarbonyl/N-methyl heterocycle and an aryl amino/oxygen-ring appendage. The initial best is already 0.167838659. Parent leaders on all seeds combine quinoline-like or related fused N-aryl chemistry with larger N-substituted dicarbonyl ring frameworks, while retaining their own irregular ring connections. In seed order 0/1/2, best observed Child scores are 0.186216711, 0.188607969, 0.186663348; published Parent best scores are 0.214451171, 0.221409546, 0.232333845. The last evaluated molecules score 0.137844713, 0.118240722, 0.162286141 in that seed order; these are final observations, not final Top-1 values.
liabilities: The best seed-1 structure contains N-Cl adjacent to an N-N/dicarbonyl system, while the best seed-0 structure contains an S-O linkage. Such motifs call for contextual chemical review rather than assuming a conventional amide or ether.

302 observations contain N-O single bonds, 57 N-halogen bonds and 24 O-O bonds; these are structural motif counts, not a classification of every matched molecule as unstable. There are also 101 tiny observations and 19 with at least 50 heavy atoms.
missing_features: The Child less consistently combines an intact aromatic framework with N-substituted carbonyl-rich rings: it has carbonyl motifs in 676/870 observations versus 855/870 in Parent, and median size 23 versus 31 heavy atoms. Neither adding carbonyls nor increasing size is proven sufficient.
Well-defined linkers and relative stereochemistry are not consistently specified; the available output does not establish a unique missing target-like scaffold.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Aromatic and carbonyl-bearing ring combinations occupy the upper Child band, whereas tiny fragments such as OCCS at seed 1 evaluation 284 score 0. The simple substituted quinoline-like terminal seed-1 molecule scores 0.118240722, below the dicarbonyl-containing leader at 0.188607969. The seed-0 ether-linked lactam/amine molecule at evaluation 26 already scores 0.182496514; its later S-O-linked leader reaches 0.186216711. Those nearby scores do not establish a benefit from the S-O linkage. Despite many different graph cores, the leaders only modestly exceed the initial best, and the observed Parent leaders all score higher.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 optimizer observations span 1-62 heavy atoms (median 19), with median two rings and zero aromatic rings. Digest ring-closure/aromatic-token incidence is 0.7874/0.477, so substantial ring content here is nonaromatic. Seed 0 leads with a 21-heavy-atom unsaturated N-methyl ring bearing an enolic carbon-centred cumulene chain and an O-alkylated hydroxyurea-like substituent. Seed 1 leads with a 25-heavy-atom sulfur/oxygen-containing unsaturated multicycle and an N-O carbonyl motif. Seed 2 leads with a 21-heavy-atom ethoxy-substituted unsaturated S/N ring attached through urea to fluoropyridyl. The common initial best is 0.002094453. Parent leaders are different N-rich carbonyl/imine heterocyclic assemblies with several fluorinated substituents, of 27, 29 and 25 heavy atoms; some also contain N-F, N-O and very small fused rings. In seed order 0/1/2, best observed Child scores are 0.313674002, 0.265898442, 0.275524288; published Parent best scores are 0.694280463, 0.499900465, 0.620122305. The last evaluated molecules score 0.198111004, 2.17207225e-16, 0.00694213557 in that seed order; these are final observations, not final Top-1 values.
liabilities: 27 observations contain carbon-centred cumulated double bonds, matching the digest text incidence of 0.031 for this task. The close seed-0 near-leader places such unsaturation within a six-membered ring, which raises a concrete geometric concern despite RDKit parsing.

The seed-1 leader contains a cyclic O-S-O connection and complex fused/bridged topology; the seed-0 leader contains an N-O urea-like group and enolic unsaturation. Reactivity, tautomeric state and synthetic access remain unmeasured. There are 102 observations with at most five heavy atoms.
missing_features: The Child does not sustain the moderately sized, multiply fluorinated N-rich ring arrangements seen among Parent leaders. It can generate fluorinated heterocycles, but its sampled best branches instead emphasize urea/N-O and unsaturated nonaromatic systems. This contrast is descriptive and does not establish a fluorination prescription.

Geometrically credible alternatives to cumulene-containing rings and fully specified stereochemical arrangements are not demonstrated for the strongest unsaturated branch; no desired target stereoisomer or particular additional group can be inferred from the scores alone.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Child improvement accompanies smaller N/O-rich ring assemblies rather than the very large early recombinations: the seed-1 evaluation-15 multiaryl/polycarbonyl product scores 3.2416258040348776e-69. Small fragments also fail: the terminal fluorinated N-chloro fragment in seed 1 scores 2.1720722460120524e-16. The seed-0 leader scores 0.313674002, and a close analogue with an additional endocyclic cumulene at evaluation 256 scores 0.312816642. A more reduced ring variant at the final evaluation scores 0.198111004. These examples show that this observed score gradient does not enforce conventional unsaturation or feasibility. Higher Parent scores coexist with different and also questionable chemistry; they do not establish a unique missing functional group.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-04741f9b1832 versus n-1744a1494180, under the registered constant-location allocation condition with original correlated residuals and inherited sulfur-gated generation, complete supplied Search seeds 0/1/2 and 300 observations per session including ten initial. Of 4350 optimizer observations per node, 612 Child versus 105 Parent structures have at most five heavy atoms, while 99 versus 48 have at least 50. Child median heavy-atom counts by the fixed session order are 22, 25, 17.5, 23 and 19, versus 24, 31, 29, 31 and 27 in Parent. The cited low-score fragments and giant recombinations coexist with substantially higher-scoring intermediate-size ring assemblies. These are current output associations; they do not identify which algorithm component caused them.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted set does not consistently preserve a useful molecular size and connected functional-group arrangement during structural variation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need to make connected, chemically interpretable alternatives around feedback-supported functional arrangements while retaining access to different sizes. Measure fragmentation, oversized recombination and preservation of useful local groups against actual subsequent accepted scores. Do not infer a universal size cutoff or import a benchmark-specific scaffold from this comparison.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Direct source n-04741f9b1832 under the registered constant-location allocation condition with original correlated residuals and inherited sulfur-gated generation on the complete frozen Search panel, with n-1744a1494180 as the same-profile comparison. SMARTS on 4350 optimizer observations give O-O/N-halogen/O-halogen counts of 224/253/207 in Child and 127/786/217 in Parent. High-scoring Child examples include a hydroperoxy aromatic analogue, an N-chloro cyclic dicarbonyl and an N-chloro amine-bearing polycycle. The direction differs by motif: the Child does not increase every alert. No stability, toxicology or synthetic-route assessment supports a blanket ban, and a permitted sulfur environment does not certify the whole molecule.
transferable_gaps.gap: Functional-group context remains insufficiently controlled: valid graphs can combine O-O, N-halogen, O-halogen and unusual heteroatom linkages even near score maxima.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and alter intact functional-group environments rather than treating heteroatom and bond substitutions as chemically interchangeable. Offer conventional alternatives preserving donor/acceptor and connectivity relationships, and evaluate their actual feedback. Any subsequent chemistry constraint would be a new tested intervention; these associations alone do not justify blacklisting all sulfur, N-O, N-N or halogen-containing molecules.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Direct re-observation in n-04741f9b1832 under the registered constant-location allocation condition with original correlated residuals and inherited sulfur-gated generation, on all three supplied Search seeds at 300 observations per session, compared with published n-1744a1494180 under the same conditions. All 4350 Child optimizer graphs parse, but 32 contain carbon-centred cumulated double bonds versus 12 in Parent; the cited high-score near-leader includes an endocyclic cumulene. Other leaders have bridged unsaturation or densely fused small rings. All Child tetrahedral-tag counts are zero while RDKit identifies unassigned potential centres in 2316 observations; Parent likewise has zero tags and 2455 observations with potential centres. These are graph-level findings, not conformer-energy or stereoisomer-stability measurements.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator produces diverse ring graphs without demonstrating credible ring geometry or complete stereochemical specification.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring edits would need awareness of ring size, unsaturation and bridge connectivity, plus preservation or resolution of stereochemistry where chemically meaningful. Distinguish a valid graph and a candidate stereocentre from a feasible conformation or isolable configuration. Assess resulting alternatives with the same task-local feedback; neither raw core novelty nor sanitization demonstrates productive chemical diversity.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
